countryCode.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code for this address, e.g. "US", "AU". Required on every postal.address -- consumers may always read countryCode without knowing which variant is present. Each variant further const-locks this to its country; a future generic international variant would keep the field open under the same pattern. Membership is not enum-enforced here (ISO list mutates; user-assigned codes such as XK are in de facto use).

description: Union of postal-address kinds. Every address carries a countryCode (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2) so consumers can always read the country without inspecting the variant -- that guarantee lives on THIS schema, not as a coincidence of the current variants. Variants are discriminated by each variant's required $kind const and further const-lock countryCode (us-address -> "US", postal.au-address -> "AU"). Composites that embed a postal address (commerce.order, billing.invoice, contact.card) $ref THIS schema, never a concrete variant directly -- so adding a new address kind (another country-specific shape, or a generic international address) is a minor version bump of postal.address alone, not a breaking revision of every composite that embeds one. Current variants: us-address (published before packages existed, so it lives at the root rather than in this package) and postal.au-address. Country-specific variants are named postal.{lowercase ISO 3166-1 alpha-2}-address (leaf slug min 3 chars blocks bare alpha-2). There is no generic international variant yet -- addresses in countries without a variant are a known gap, next in line as demand shows up. Discriminator (OpenAPI-style; enable in AJV with discriminator: true) uses $kind so validators apply only the matching oneOf arm.
title: Postal address
